title: Paged KV cache: block allocator reuse, locality-aware pinning and manager refactor
author: Evelyn Chen
description: Motivation: reduce fragmentation and contention in the paged KV cache by reworking the block allocator and block manager. This PR introduces allocator reuse semantics, a locality-aware pinning policy, and a manager refactor to separate lifecycle and eviction concerns. Key goals: 1) reduce allocation churn under heavy streaming workloads, 2) improve cache hit locality for multi-tenant workloads, 3) simplify the manager surface for easier reasoning and future policies. Summary of changes: refactor BlockAllocator into a BlockPool interface with explicit Acquire/Release semantics, implement an LRU+Locality pinning policy that prefers reusing blocks on the same GPU node where possible, add a lightweight BlockBorrower concept to allow transient pins during scheduling, implement allocator reuse pools to avoid repeated mmap/munmap cycles, add TTL-aware eviction hooks to prevent unnecessary churn for recently-used KV pages, add a microbench harness and unit tests covering reuse/pinning edge cases, add metrics for allocation latency, eviction count, and pin locality. Compatibility notes: this is an internal refactor with no external API changes. There are conservative fallbacks in the manager to the previous eviction strategy when locality information is unavailable. Testing and benchmarks: included unit tests, integration tests in perf-canary, and microbench results attached showing up to 18% reduction in p99 allocation latency and a 12% improvement in overall token throughput for chat workloads with large KV footprints. Link to benchmark artifacts: linear/ENG-7182/benchmarks. See release notes for user-facing impact and rollout plan.
